fields.title: الاحساء کی قومی تفریح گاہ
fields.summary: ایک مصنوعی جنگل، جو 1962 کے ریت روکنے کے منصوبے سے وجود میں آیا۔ یہاں جھاؤ کے لاکھوں درخت، سائبان اور پیدل چلنے کے راستے ہیں۔
fields.body: الاحساء کے نخلستان کے شمال مشرق میں، العمران شہر کے پاس اور جبل القارہ کے قریب، الاحساء کی قومی تفریح گاہ پھیلی ہوئی ہے۔ اس کی کہانی 1382 ہجری (1962 عیسوی) میں زراعت کی وزارت کے ایک منصوبے سے شروع ہوئی۔ مقصد اس ریت کو روکنا تھا جو نخلستان کے دیہات پر چڑھتی چلی آ رہی تھی۔ یہاں تقریباً 4,500 ہیکٹر کے رقبے پر اور بیس کلومیٹر لمبی ایک پٹی میں لاکھوں درخت لگائے گئے، جن میں زیادہ تر جھاؤ کے تھے۔ ریت روکنے والی یہ باڑیں وقت کے ساتھ ساتھ ایک ہرا بھرا مصنوعی جنگل بن گئیں، اور پھر ایک عوامی تفریح گاہ، جہاں سائبان، پیدل چلنے کے راستے اور خاندانوں کے لیے سہولتیں ہیں۔ آج اس کی نگرانی سبزے کے فروغ اور صحرا کے پھیلاؤ کی روک تھام کا قومی مرکز کرتا ہے، جو اس تفریح گاہ کی بحالی کے منصوبے جاری رکھے ہوئے ہے۔ اسی تفریح گاہ کی حدود میں نمک برداشت کرنے والی مقامی اقسام کے بیس لاکھ درختوں کے ساتھ جواثا کے جنگل کا آغاز کیا گیا۔
fields.area: العمران، نخلستان کے شمال مشرق میں

accuracy.why: Read against both sources leaf by leaf. The story of 1382 AH / 1962 CE and the ministry's project; the sand creeping over the oasis villages; some 4,500 hectares and a belt of twenty kilometres, joined as the Arabic joins them; most of the trees tamarisk in the body, all in the summary, each as its source; the barriers that became a forest and then a public park; shades by the Arabic (the English-only 'seating' is not written, logged); the centre and its rehabilitation projects of the park; the forest launched with two million trees of salt-tolerant native species, the number in words as both sources have it (change 2). The oasis is named once (ruling N47). Two points off: 'millions of trees' is said with the Urdu scale word in its plural, which by the letter says hundreds of thousands (ruling P10 leaves no other idiom); and the centre's name is a description that narrows 'vegetation cover' to greenery (item N110).

nativeness.why: On one reader, who gave this page the most remarks of the six. WHAT STANDS AND COSTS: the title, which he did not recognise as a national park (moderate; ruling N69's noun); the adjective of the forest, 'fake' on first pass (moderate; the reference's own term, kept); two possessives with the year in the summary (minor); the barriers, for which he looked back (minor); the centre's description, twelve words long, and the participle he calls office language. CURED, AND UNREAD: the order of the centre's sentence, the pronoun, the verb of launching (changes 0, 1 and 3) — three edits in the paragraph's last two sentences, charged as unknown, not as sound. The first four sentences of the body drew no remark on their wording.

compliance.why: Letterforms and digits clean (the checker, the proof scan of stage 5; the changed strings scanned by the build script). Names equal to their keys; the oasis and the mountain as approved; the year pair as ruling N12; the clock form; the two approved labels and the fee pair. One point off: the title, the city, the forest, the ministry and the centre are pending entries, none attested in Urdu.

fit.why: One point off for the Urdu's own share: the reader of the title and of the first line does not learn that this is the national park until the paragraph, and pictures a fake forest for a moment. That the page gives no entrance for a strip twenty kilometres long, no facilities, says 'rehabilitation' and no more, and does not say whether the two million trees are planted: the source's, logged, not charged.

fields.summary: تاریخی مسجد جواثا کے پہلو میں ایک سرسبز تفریح گاہ، جو خاندان کے ساتھ گھومنے پھرنے کی جگہ ہے۔

fields.title: عین النجم کی تفریح گاہ
fields.summary: المبرز کے مغرب میں تاریخی عین نجم کے گرد بنی ایک تفریح گاہ۔ الاحساء کے گندھک والے شفا بخش چشموں میں عین نجم سب سے مشہور ہے۔
fields.body: المبرز کے مغرب میں عین النجم کی تفریح گاہ واقع ہے۔ یہ ایک عوامی تفریح گاہ ہے جو الاحساء کی بلدیہ نے عین نجم نامی تاریخی چشمے کے گرد بنائی ہے۔ یہ چشمہ الاحساء کے گندھک والے مشہور ترین گرم چشموں میں سے ایک ہے۔ لوگ قدیم زمانے سے اس کے شفا بخش پانی کے لیے یہاں آتے رہے ہیں، اور کہا جاتا ہے کہ یہ سعودی عرب میں شفایابی کے لیے مخصوص پہلا سیاحتی مقام ہے۔ اس چشمے کی عمارتیں، جن کے نیم بیضوی گنبد ان کی پہچان ہیں، 1115 ہجری (1703 عیسوی) میں تعمیر ہوئیں۔ یہ چشمہ اس علاقے کی تاریخ سے جڑا ہوا ہے: 1799 میں الاحساء کے لوگوں نے اسی کے پاس سعود بن عبد العزیز کے ہاتھ پر بیعت کی، جو بعد میں امام بنے، اور 1367 ہجری (1948 عیسوی) میں شاہ عبد العزیز اس کے پانی سے علاج کے لیے یہاں آئے۔ ترقیاتی کاموں کے بعد یہ تفریح گاہ 2015 کے وسط میں سیاحوں کے لیے کھول دی گئی۔ یہاں ہریالی ہے اور خاندان کے ساتھ مل بیٹھنے کی پرسکون جگہیں ہیں۔ آج اس کا انتظام الاحساء کی بلدیہ سنبھالتی ہے۔

fields.title: الشیبانی / المشقر کی تفریح گاہ
fields.summary: القارہ گاؤں کے قریب ایک وسیع تفریح گاہ، جس کا نام زمانہ جاہلیت کے قلعہ المشقر کے نام پر ہے۔ اس کے قلب میں ایک محل ہے جو اسی قلعے سے متاثر ہو کر بنایا گیا۔
fields.body: الاحساء کے نخلستان کے مشرقی حصے میں، القارہ گاؤں کے قریب، المشقر کی تفریح گاہ پھیلی ہوئی ہے، جو پہلے الشیبانی کی تفریح گاہ کہلاتی تھی۔ گھنے پیڑ پودوں میں گھری یہ ایک ہری بھری جگہ ہے، جہاں کھلے سبزہ زار، ایک عوامی بازار اور خاندانوں کے لیے کھیل کی جگہیں ہیں۔ اس جگہ کا نام زمانہ جاہلیت کے مشہور قلعہ المشقر کے نام پر ہے۔ قدیم عربی تحریروں میں اسے “قلعہ ہجر” کہا گیا ہے۔ اس کا ذکر عربوں کی ان مشہور لڑائیوں کے تذکروں میں آتا ہے جو “ایام العرب” کہلاتی ہیں۔ اسی کے پڑوس میں سوق المشقر نامی بازار لگتا تھا، جو زمانہ جاہلیت میں عربوں کے بازاروں میں سے ایک تھا۔ البتہ اصل قلعہ کہاں تھا، اس پر محققین میں آج بھی اختلاف ہے: کوئی اسے البطالیہ میں بتاتا ہے، کوئی جواثا میں اور کوئی القارہ میں۔ تفریح گاہ کے قلب میں “قصر المشقر” کھڑا ہے۔ یہ ایک جدید عمارت ہے، جو اس قدیم قلعے سے متاثر ہو کر بنائی گئی۔ اب یہی اس تفریح گاہ کا مرکز اور اس کی پہچان ہے۔

fields.summary: الشعبہ/کنزان کے پہاڑی سلسلے پر ایک پہاڑی تفریح گاہ، جو الاحساء کی بلدیہ بنا رہی ہے۔ یہاں پہاڑی ڈھلان پر پھسلنے کی جگہیں، معلق پل اور آبشار ہیں۔

fields.title: الکوت کی تفریح گاہ
fields.summary: ہفوف کے تاریخی مرکز میں بلدیہ کا ایک باغ، جو قصر ابراہیم سے چند قدم کے فاصلے پر ہے اور “شہروں کو لوگوں کے لیے بہتر بنانے” کے منصوبے کا حصہ ہے۔
fields.body: ہفوف کے تاریخی مرکز میں، محلہ الکوت کے قلب میں، الکوت کی تفریح گاہ واقع ہے۔ یہاں سے چند قدم کے فاصلے پر سوق القیصریہ نامی بازار اور قصر ابراہیم ہیں۔ یہ بلدیہ کا ایک باغ ہے، جس کا افتتاح الاحساء کی بلدیہ نے 2020 کے اواخر میں کیا۔ یہ ان آٹھ باغوں میں سے ایک ہے جو “شہروں کو لوگوں کے لیے بہتر بنانے” کے منصوبے میں شامل ہیں۔ اس باغ میں فوارے، درخت اور سبزہ زار ہیں، اور بچوں کے کھیلنے کی ایک سایہ دار جگہ بھی۔ یہاں چہل قدمی کے راستے اور عوامی بیت الخلا ہیں، اور معذور افراد کی ضروریات کا خیال رکھا گیا ہے۔ یہ باغ ان منصوبوں کے وسیع تر سلسلے کا بھی حصہ ہے جو ہفوف کے تاریخی مرکز کی ترقی کے لیے ہیں۔ ان منصوبوں میں اس محلے کے باغوں کو الاحساء کے طرز تعمیر کا رنگ دیا جا رہا ہے۔ یوں یہ باغ قدرتی طور پر محلے کے ورثے کے مقامات کے درمیان دم لینے کی جگہ بن جاتا ہے۔
fields.area: محلہ الکوت، ہفوف کے وسط میں

accuracy.why: In the heart of the district, in the historic centre of the town; steps from the palace and the market, in the approved baiah sentence; a municipal garden inaugurated by the municipality in late 2020, by the Arabic's verb; one of eight gardens of the programme, whose noun is the Arabic's; fountains, trees and lawns, a shaded play area, walkways and public toilets by the Arabic, the needs of people with disabilities; part of the wider set of projects; the district's gardens given the colour of Al-Ahsa's building style. Two points off: 'a natural pause' is said in one of its two senses, the English's (change 14); and 'motifs' is carried by an idiom of colour that says less (item N115).

nativeness.why: The reader calls the middle of the paragraph 'the most useful passage in all six pages'. WHAT STANDS AND COSTS: the programme's name, strange as a name (moderate; a planning term neither source explains); three possessives round the heritage landmarks (forced by ruling N58); the chain 'the wider set of projects … which are for the development of' (the source's press-release sentence, the Urdu's chain); the title's noun against the text's and the card's gender (minor; the English's switch). CURED, AND UNREAD: the historic centre, three times, the summary's chain and the word that misled him (changes 10 to 14).

compliance.why: Letterforms clean; the feminine string of ruling N65 byte for byte, by the gender of the title's entry; the area line the approved pair; the market with the particle of naming, first in its list of two; the palace bare (ruling P3c); the programme's name in its marks with the noun outside (ruling N16). One point off: the title and the programme are pending.

fit.why: One point off for the Urdu's own share: in the one line under the title a six-word programme name takes the place of what the garden is like, and a traveller meets a feminine card over a masculine text. That the title says a park and the text a garden, and that the closing sentences tell nothing one could picture: the source's, logged, not charged.

structure.why: Nine leaves in pack order; two rows; two pairs of marks, closed; the Hours value a full sentence without a final stop, as ruling N65 fixes it; no notice line, the page being an open site (the template's rule).

blind_reader_rulings.reason: The notice is the approved interface string det.hoursNotice, not a leaf of this batch; it names the management and the template shows no contact on these pages (none of the six sources carries a phone or a site; operatorUrl is false on all six). Logged for the owner with the interface defects: an instruction the reader cannot follow.

Interface string trails.partOf, approved in b0-ui and not a leaf. FIVE READERS OF FIVE have now read 'roads' first (four in b6, this one). On this page the list under it is in English (the template links the English trail; stage 4's note). For the interface round, with the reader's wording on record.

The noun is ruling N69's and the loan stays out under the owner's rule on loans (P16); neither is reopened by a batch judge, and the remark is graded minor. The category label is the approved interface label. ON RECORD FOR THE OWNER, since the entry of the noun itself says the loan 'would have to pass the loan test … there' on a park page: this reader, like the readers of b1, b2 and b6, says the everyday word is the loan, and for 'national park' he did not recognise the native wording (item 11). The question is put to the owner in the notes; the text keeps the ruled noun.
Approved interface heading of b0-ui (det.nearby.h), not a leaf. A second reader finds it louder than the text around it (b6's fourth reader said 'an advertisement'). For the interface round.
Approved interface string, not a leaf. Understood on a second reading; his wording adds a statement about the road that the string does not make. For the interface round, on record.
Approved interface string (ruling N4), shown only after the location is refused; not a leaf. The loan he offers is on the owner's refused list (ruling P16-test). On record.

None of the six sources says whether there is a place to pray, toilets (koot-park excepted), food, parking or shade, and no card has such a row. Nothing is supplied. Logged for the owner, with the reader's sentence: after reading he cannot judge how long a family could stay.

The mix is the sources', field by field: 'twenty kilometres', 'eight gardens', 'three suspended bridges', 'two lakes' and 'two million' are words in both languages, '4,500', '1,100' and '1,500' figures; a year stands in both calendars where the source gives both and bare where it gives one (ruling N12: nothing is converted and nothing computed). The Urdu keeps each as its source has it. One form moved in this round and moves the Urdu TOWARDS its sources: the two million of national-park is in words again (change 2, item N104).

The word for family is the owner's decision of 2026-10-12 (ruling P16: the native word, not the loan) and is approved text on king-abdullah-park, salwa-beach and jabal-al-qarah; graded minor. That the pages do not say WHICH family facilities is the sources' ('family facilities', 'family play areas'). Recorded for whoever reopens P16: one more reader says the loan.

Each of the three is the source's own image ('at its heart', 'At the park's heart', 'In the heart of the Al-Koot district'; the Arabic has the same noun three times) and the wording is approved text for exactly this (qasr-ibrahim, sahood, abubakr-mosque, jabal-al-qarah). On koot-park his alternative would stand twice in one clause, next to the word for the town's centre. Minor; charged under nativeness on mushaqar, where it stands twice.

What he asks for is the loan, in the title. The noun is ruling N69's and the pattern is the line's for a place named after a place (item N101, ruled A); a batch judge reopens neither. The cost is real and is charged on this page under nativeness and under fit: he did not recognise the place as a national park until well into the paragraph. Evidence read by the judge (ur.wikipedia exact phrase, HTTP 200): the loan compound on 1306 pages, the native adjective with the loan noun on 701, the wording in the title on 1. FOR THE OWNER, as a decision and not a mere option (notes): whether a national park, and a park at all, takes the loan on /ur/.

The phrase is a verified termbase entry and the reference's own term for exactly this kind of forest: the lead of the article on Changa Manga (ur.wikipedia, HTTP 200, read by the judge) calls it by these two words and, in the next sentence, 'the largest forest planted by human hands' — the best-known planted forest of the reader's own country. He corrected himself inside the sentence ('as the paragraph shows'). A sourced entry is not overruled on one self-corrected first impression. Charged under nativeness (moderate, one reader). ON RECORD, if a second reader pictures a fake forest: his wording for the summary alone, which says 'planted' where the summary's sources say 'man-made' / 'artificial' and would be counted as a word from the body.

His wording moves the year from the project to the forest ('which came into being in 1962'): both sources date the PROJECT ('born of a 1962 sand-control project'), and the body says the forest grew 'over time'. The two possessives are how Urdu attaches a year and a purpose to one noun; no order of them is shorter without that shift. Minor; charged under nativeness.

Item N110, ruled A for the ministry. Ruling N98 names this very phrase 'by itself the ordinary Urdu for a ministry of agriculture' and leaves the one-field case to this page; the line builds every named body with the Urdu possessive and the noun last (rulings N44, N68, N98), and the site's two ministries are then built alike. He calls it grammatical and grades it minor. His order is the reference's (36 pages against 0, HTTP 200) and is the OWNER'S one-line option. Said plainly for the coordinator: his order could also not be entered cleanly — the key it replaces is a run of whole words inside asfar's approved name of the other ministry, and a retired key is searched in every batch's text (notes).

Both sources give the two measures side by side and do not say how they relate: 'over an area of some 4,500 hectares with a belt running twenty kilometres'; the Arabic joins them with 'and'. The Urdu's conjunction is the Arabic's. His wording makes the belt and the area one and the same, which neither source states. The unit is the sources'. Logged.

The noun renders 'the sand barriers' (the Arabic's 'sand-breaks'), and the demonstrative ties it to the trees just planted. His wording ('rows of trees planted to stop the sand') adds rows that no source has. Minor; charged under nativeness: he looked back for a fence.

Applied by re-ordering (change 0): what is overseen comes first, so the long description of the centre is met as the answer to 'by whom', as in both sources. No marks round the name (ruling N16). The centre's description is still twelve words long (item N110: plain words for a body nobody names in Urdu) and the participle he calls office language is the source's 'continues its … projects'; both are charged.

Both sources say 'rehabilitation projects' and nothing more — not what is rehabilitated, not whether anything is closed for it — under a card that says open daily. The Urdu noun is the plain word for rehabilitation. Nothing is supplied. Logged.

Applied in the two parts that are the Urdu's own: the pronoun is replaced by the noun it stands for (change 1) and the forest is 'launched' in the nominal frame Urdu uses for it (change 3). NOT applied: 'planted' — both sources say 'launched … with two million trees' and neither says the trees are in the ground, or when; and how this Jawatha Forest lies to the Jawatha of the next page is said by no source (logged, as stage 4 logged it).
The area line is the source's ('Al-Omran — northeast of the oasis'); no source says where one enters a strip twenty kilometres long or where the shades are. Nothing is supplied. Logged.

The word is the dictionary's for the tamarisk (verified entry: its dictionary page and the reference article, whose lead gives the Arabic name of this very tree), and the text says they are trees. No other Urdu word names the tree. Minor; recorded in the entry.

Both sources say of the park itself only 'a broad green park' and 'a fitting destination for family outings'; everything else in the paragraph is about what stands beside it. Nothing is supplied. Logged for the owner: the page charges a fee and does not say what is inside.
The sentence is the sources' own ('joining nature to history', the same in the Arabic), translated word for word; its register is not traded for content (ruling P24). Logged.

The clause after the colon is the owner's guarded claim (build check C30), byte for byte the approved jawatha-mosque wording, and is not touched in this batch. Its three features are each a ruled form: the colon before what explains the mosque (ruling N33), the city with its epithet beside the mosque where the English names it (ruling P9), and 'place' for the source's 'the first place'. Minor. Recorded for the owner with the claim: a reader finds the city superfluous and expects 'mosque' for 'place'.

This page's sources say nothing about praying in the mosque or about women; the mosque has its own approved page, with its owner-fixed visiting row. 'Visiting the mosque is free' is the source's fee note in the word ruling N17 gives a mosque. Nothing is supplied here. Logged: the park page is where a family meets the mosque first, and it does not send them to the mosque's page.

What the site is — ruins, a dig, a museum — and whether one may walk in, neither source says ('the Jawatha archaeological site', the same three words in the Arabic). The two possessives are the plain build of the three words; the more natural Urdu name-form for such a place says 'the antiquities of Jawatha', which tells the reader that remains are to be seen — more than the sources say — so it is not written. It is on record for the owner beside the defect. The chain is charged under nativeness (moderate, one reader).

The sentence is in both sources ('opening hours and fees are listed in the visit-information card below'); it is worded as ruling N89 words such a sentence, with the interface heading quoted exactly. That it reads as filler is the source's. Logged.

Neither source says who pays 10 and who 15, whether per person or per car, or why a range ('SAR 10–15 · visiting the mosque is free'; the Arabic likewise). The amount is written as rulings P7 and N13 give a range of two figures, with the currency's full name once in the field; the middle dot is the source's, as on the approved fee row of the mosque page. Nothing is supplied. Logged prominently: a family cannot work out the cost.

The four questions and their answers are the source's, in both languages, and repeat its card and its body; the third question is the source's ('What is next to Jawatha Park?'). Translated as they are. Logged.

Each area line keeps its own source's reference point: Hofuf here ('Al-Kilabiyah — northeast of Hofuf'), the oasis on national-park and kanzan-park. The sources do not say how the two relate. Logged (the cost ruling N30 states).

THE TWO SPELLINGS are the Arabic's: the title has the article inside the spring's name, the summary and the body name the spring without it (bold, where it is named for itself); the English has one spelling throughout. Arabic is the only source of name spellings, so the Urdu carries each as its field's Arabic has it, and which of the two is the name is the OWNER'S to say: new item N117 (owner_decision), with the judge's recommendation. Not settled silently. THE SUMMARY'S FIRST LINE: his wording sets the Urdu generic next to the name, which rulings P3c and P3c-labels bar in a summary (the name stands bare there; the second sentence of the summary says it is a spring, and the body introduces it with its generic). That the first word of the name reads as the adverb is the known cost of such names (ruling P18 keeps the adverb off the page); charged under nativeness and fit.

Confirmed against both languages: the summary says 'the most famous of Al-Ahsa's healing sulphur springs', the body 'one of Al-Ahsa's most famous hot sulphur springs'; the Arabic has the same two statements. Each field keeps its own source (the German and Russian lines did the same). Logged.

SERIOUS, and the source's — confirmed against the English and the Arabic of every sentence he quotes. Both say the spring was 'sought since old times for its healing waters' (the Arabic verb with 'since antiquity'), report it as a tourist site 'devoted to healing' in the present, and then describe the park by 'greenery and quiet family sittings'; neither says whether there is water today, whether one may bathe, or how. The Urdu's perfect of habit ('have been coming since old times') is what 'since' says in both; a past tense would assert that the visits stopped, which no source says either. Nothing is supplied and nothing softened. LOGGED FIRST among the batch's defects: a family would arrive expecting a hot-spring bath.

Applied (change 4): the reporting verb of the approved pages, with the claim's superlative and its restriction kept. His own sentence is not written: it changes the tense of the visits and drops 'tourist site devoted to', and how the site reports a claim is not the translation's to change (ruling P25).

Which buildings a spring has, and whether they still stand, neither source says ('Its buildings, with their distinctive half-oval domes, were raised in 1115 AH / 1703 CE'; in the Arabic they are the spring's). The adjective is the source's 'half-oval', word for word. Nothing is supplied. Logged.

Three things, each the source's. (a) 1799 stands in one calendar in both languages between two years given in both; ruling N12 keeps a one-calendar year bare, converts nothing and computes nothing. (b) 'Later Imam' is the source's bracket; the Urdu is the approved wording of the same words on muhairis, and a gloss of the title would be a fact no source of the page gives. (c) Two men named with Abdulaziz stand in one sentence in both sources. Logged; for the owner: a Hijri year for the pledge, as the approved muhairis and khuzam pages date the same man's acts.
Both sources name the municipality twice in the paragraph ('laid out by Al-Ahsa Municipality … it is managed today by Al-Ahsa Municipality'). Minor. Logged.

Two ruled forms. The area line opens with the larger place as a bare name because this source names one ('West of Al-Mubarraz — Al-Ahsa'; ruling P20); the other five sources name none. The half hour is written as ruling N23 gives it, and that ruling records his very wording as the option for whoever reopens P13: he is one more reader for it. Minor.

The title mirrors title_en ('Al-Shaibani / Al-Mushaqar Park': the former name first, a slash, the present name, the generic), as the style rule for titles asks and as the German and Russian lines did; the Arabic title is the present name alone, and both bodies name the park by its present name. The reader shows what the English title costs: two places, or a person and a park. Which title the page carries is the OWNER'S DECISION — item N112 (owner_decision), with the judge's recommendation for the present name alone. Until he answers the title stands as the source has it; logged with the page's defects.

The three nouns are the sources': 'a palace' in the summary, the quoted name 'Mushaqar Palace' and 'a modern building' in the body. What it is used for and whether one may enter, neither says. The Urdu's own share is small and ruled: the common noun in the summary is the Urdu word for a palace, the name keeps its Arabic generic (ruling N14; item N113), so one Arabic word is two Urdu words on the page. Charged under nativeness; logged.

'A folk souq' is all either source says (the Arabic: a popular market) — not what is sold or when. The adjective is the Urdu for the Arabic's word. 'Family play areas' here and 'children's play areas' on kanzan-park are the two sources' own wordings. Nothing is supplied. Logged.

Applied for the frame and the noun (change 5): the fort 'is called' so in old Arabic writings, with the approved shaban page's noun for the old sources. THE MISREADING ITSELF STANDS and is open item N7, which bites here for the second time on the site: the second word of the quoted name is letter for letter the Urdu word for separation. A vowel sign is barred (rulings P8 and P17), a word saying what Hajar was would be a fact no leaf of the page carries, and the generic twice in four words was refused at stage 2. Charged under fit on this page; FOR THE OWNER: one clause in the source saying what Hajar was.

The clause is the source's, word for word: 'one of the pre-Islamic Arab fairs', the Arabic 'one of the markets of the Arabs in the pre-Islamic age' — a set term for the famous fairs, which neither source explains. A word such as 'famous' would be added. Logged.
The balance is the sources': both give the fort four of their sentences and the park two. He calls the history well written. Logged.

The marks follow one rule: a name that both sources set in quotation marks stands in them (the fort's second name and the modern building's name; rulings N40 and N72, item N113), and a term cited as what something is called stands in them (ruling N16, point 5; item N107). The fort's and the market's own names are names in use and stand bare, as every approved page has such names. Minor.

The gallery heading and the image's alternative text are interface strings and the template's build (the title and an interface word), not leaves; the page has one image. For the interface round: a plural heading over one picture.

The name is written letter for letter as the Arabic writes it, with its article; no vowel sign and no gloss for pronunciation is added (ruling P17). Recorded in the entry, as for the names two batches before it. Minor.

SERIOUS, and the source's — confirmed against both languages. The summary says the municipality 'is building' the park and lists what is there; the body says partial operation of the upper section began in late 2022 and ends, in the English only, 'full operation is yet to be confirmed'; the card gives daily hours and free entry as verified, in both languages. The Arabic body has no closing reservation at all. The Urdu carries each statement at its own strength and ties the listed things to the upper section, as the source does. Nothing is evened out. LOGGED SECOND among the batch's defects: he would not take the children.

The names are the sources': the title names the park after Kanzan with the present-day name in a bracket, the summary joins the two names with a slash, the body says the official name is another, and the card names the mountain by its present-day name — in both languages. The bracket stays (item N103). 'The massif of Al-Shu'bah Mountain' is said with the approved wording of the kanzan page for the massif, and 'this mountain' with that page's own possessive (item N108); that a massif is spoken of as a mountain is the sources'. Logged; for the owner: one name in the title.

Applied in the part that is the Urdu's own (change 6): one wording on the page, without the noun for level ground. What the thing is, neither source says ('mountain slides', the Arabic's word also means skiing). Logged.

Applied (change 7): the measure is the length the falls extend over, as both sources give it, and the participle shows that there are several. That waterfalls have a length of more than a kilometre is the sources' statement. Logged.

Applied for the cable car (change 8): the loan, under the three conditions of ruling P16-test, with the evidence in item N106. NOT applied for the zipline: he decoded the description rightly, nothing guarded hangs on it, the loan has no dictionary entry and thin attestation, and the Arabic source itself describes the ride ('the flying rope'). The description stands and what the ride is called is the OWNER'S decision — new item N116 (owner_decision), with the judge's recommendation for the loan. With one ride named, the two can no longer be mixed up. Charged under nativeness and fit.
Applied (change 8): the two sentences are one, as in both sources; no finite verb now says that the announced cable car exists.

Applied for the doubled adverb (change 9). The rest is the English source's own reservation, which has no Arabic: 'the remaining construction phases are still under way, and full operation is yet to be confirmed' can be read both ways in the English too. How the site states a reservation of its own is not the translation's to change (ruling P25; items N99 and N109). Logged.

The page's category is 'nature' in its source file, the other five are 'parks'; the breadcrumb, the label above the title and the back link are approved interface strings chosen by that field. Not leaves. Logged for the owner: a built park with rides filed under natural sites.
The card says 'Free entry' in both languages and no source says whether the rides and the slides are free. Nothing is supplied. Logged.

Applied for the chain in the summary (change 11: 'part of' the programme, as the summary's English says). The name itself stays: it is the planning term in the plain words of ruling N79, inside the marks ruling N16 gives a programme's short name (item N111); both sources quote it and neither explains it. That it sounds strange as a name is charged under nativeness and fit, and the literal name is on record for the owner.
Applied in all three places (changes 10, 12 and 13): the reference's wording for a historic centre (item N118).

The switch is the English source's: 'Al-Koot Park' in its title, 'a municipal garden', 'The garden' in its text; the Arabic has the garden noun throughout, title included. The Urdu title mirrors title_en (the style rule for titles; item N102, ruled A), the text follows the text, and the card's feminine is ruling N65's choice by the gender of the title's entry. The municipality stands twice in one sentence in the English too. Minor. Logged, with the garden title as the owner's option.

A palace name met in passing stands bare (ruling P3c, point 2: its generic is an Urdu word), and a summary carries no gloss; the name stands bare in approved text on baiah and jabri-mosque, and the place has its own page. Minor.

The two sentences are the sources' ('It also falls within the wider set of projects to develop historic central Hofuf, where the district's gardens are being styled with Hasawi architectural motifs'), and their register is theirs; what one would see, neither says. Worded as item N115 rules. The Urdu's share — a chain of possessives in the first of them — is charged under nativeness. Logged.

Applied for the word that misled him (change 14: the adverb, and the verb of becoming). The three possessives before it are forced by ruling N58 and stay; his own sentence replaces heritage landmarks by historic buildings, which that ruling refuses.

The Hours value is one of the two fixed strings of ruling N65, byte for byte, chosen by the gender of the title's entry; a full sentence by that ruling. The notice is absent because the page is an open site (build checks C12 and C13): the template's rule, not a leaf. Minor. His praise of the paragraph's middle is recorded: 'the most useful passage in all six pages'.

source_defects.where: najm-park: summary and body — the healing spring (reader item 33, SERIOUS; items 32, 35)
source_defects.defect: The page is about a hot sulphur spring 'sought since old times for its healing waters' and reported as 'the Kingdom's first tourist site devoted to healing', and then describes a park by 'greenery and quiet family sittings'. Neither language says whether the spring has water today, whether one may bathe, or what arrangements there are. The summary says THE most famous spring, the body ONE OF the most famous. Which buildings the spring has and whether they stand is not said.
source_defects.effect_on_urdu: Each statement carried at its own strength and tense ('since old times' as a perfect of habit; the claim reported). Nothing supplied, nothing softened. HARM: a family would arrive expecting a hot-spring bath. FOR THE OWNER: one sentence saying what a visitor finds at the spring today; one of the two superlatives.

source_defects.where: kanzan-park: summary, body and card — is it open? (reader item 48, SERIOUS; items 53, 54, 56)
source_defects.defect: The summary says the park is being built and lists what is there; the body says partial operation of the upper section began in late 2022 and, in the English only, that 'full operation is yet to be confirmed' (the Arabic body ends before it and 'remaining' is English-only); the card gives daily hours and free entry as verified. The approved kanzan page says the mountain is open 24 hours; neither page says how the two relate. No source says whether the rides are free.
source_defects.effect_on_urdu: Each statement carried as its source has it; the listed things tied to the upper section, as in the source; the announced cable car and lakes kept as announced, with no verb that says they exist (change 8). The reservation worded on ruling N99's predicate (item N109). HARM: he would not take the children. FOR THE OWNER: what is open today, in the body and in the card; the reservation in the Arabic too if it stays.

source_defects.where: kanzan-park: title, summary, body, card — the names (reader item 49); the category (item 55)
source_defects.defect: The title names the park after Kanzan with the mountain's present-day name in a bracket; the English title says 'Adventure' where the Arabic says 'Mountain'; the summary joins the two names with a slash; the body says the project is officially known by another name; the card uses the present-day name. A massif is spoken of as a mountain. The page is filed under 'nature', the other five parks under 'parks'.
source_defects.effect_on_urdu: Title built from the Arabic name with the approved key of the mountain and the bracket both source titles carry (item N103); the slash and the official name as the sources have them. FOR THE OWNER: one name in the title; the page's category.

source_defects.where: najm-park: title against summary and body — the spring's name (reader item 31); the pledge of 1799 (item 36)
source_defects.defect: The Arabic title has the article inside the spring's name; the Arabic summary and body name the spring without it. The English has one spelling. The Arabic title's generic is the garden noun, the English says 'Park' and both bodies 'a public park'. The pledge of 1799 has no Hijri year, between two years given in both calendars, where two approved pages date the same man's acts in both. 'And wellness' is English-only on a reported claim; the English 'Its buildings' points at the park, the Arabic at the spring.

Its title: a quoted Arabic word that is letter for letter an Urdu word. «ہجر» (Hajar, the historical region) is letter for letter the Urdu «ہجر», 'separation from the beloved' — rekhtadictionary.com/meaning-of-hijr (HTTP 200): «ہِجْر … اسم، مذکر — محبوب سے دوری، جدائی، فراق».
